summary: Brian frames this video around his thesis that healthy businesses with big pullbacks are the opportunity — using Palantir, down 54% five weeks after a 2022 investment that later grew $10,000 to over $115,000. He runs four stocks through three checks: free cash flow, sales growth, and stable-or-rising operating margin. GE Vernova passes all three: $12.4B TTM free cash flow (up from $2.7B; $6.4B is customer turbine prepayments the bears distrust, but the 116 GW order book backs it), sales +13%, margin 1.9% to 4.4%, still 19% below its high — his ladder of $1,100-$1,300 says the drop merits re-reading the business, which he found unbroken. Uber passes all three: $10B free cash flow (+19%), sales +17%, margin 9.5% to 12.5%, 28% below its high; the weight is Waymo ending its partnership (Phoenix done June 2026, Austin possibly after 2028) and Uber's ~$10B autonomy commitments. PayPal fails the margin check (16.4%, down 1.7 points on deliberate branded-checkout spend) but posts $6.6B free cash flow (+25%) and 6% sales growth, 32% below its high after Stripe's $60.50/share bid fell through — his ladder says buy. Intuitive Surgical passes all three (sales +21%, margin 28% to 31%, $3.2B free cash flow +62%) but J&J's newly FDA-cleared Otava robot is a real competitor and shorts grew — his ladder says wait for $333. Calls: GEV BUY; UBER BUY; PYPL BUY; ISRG CONDITIONAL_BUY.
title: If You Missed Palantir at $25... It's Happening Again
